note: Every number below is a deliberately simplified, labeled-fictional model for a dramatization. None of this is a real cryptographic estimate.
quantum_note: Grover's algorithm gives a real quadratic speedup against brute-force search (256 -> 128 effective bits). The dramatization is pretending a quantum computer at that scale exists, not the math itself.
expected_attempts_note: Brute force is expected to succeed after searching about half the keyspace on average.
baseline_note: Starting 'AI compute' is pinned near the order of magnitude of the entire Bitcoin network's current hash rate (~10^21 H/s), used purely as an illustrative anchor so the slider has a relatable starting line.
growth_model: compute(t) = baseline * 2^(t / doubling_period); cumulative attempts = integral of compute(t) from 0 to crack time
reality_check: At today's baseline compute with zero growth, brute-forcing SHA-256 would take on the order of 10^38 times the current age of the universe. Real SHA-256 brute force is considered infeasible for any foreseeable computer.
